cards.name: Jerusalem
cards.line: Jerusalem is a mountain city, also called the city of David and the holy city, where God's temple stood and where the Bible's kings, prophets, and Jesus all came.

moments.title: David plans for the temple
moments.text: David called Israel's leaders to Jerusalem. He told them God had chosen his son Solomon, not David, to build the house for God's Name.

moments.title: The LORD saves Jerusalem
moments.text: The Assyrians shouted against the God of Jerusalem. Hezekiah and Isaiah prayed, and the LORD sent an angel, saved the people, and gave them rest on every side.

moments.title: Ezra arrives safely
moments.text: Ezra and the people set out for Jerusalem, and the hand of God protected them from enemies and bandits on the way. They arrived and rested there for three days.

moments.title: Jesus visits the pool
moments.text: Jesus went up to Jerusalem for a feast. Near the Sheep Gate, at the pool called Bethesda, He saw a man who had been ill for thirty-eight years and told him to get up and walk.

cards.name: Egypt
cards.line: Egypt is the land of the Nile, where Abram fled a famine and Jacob's family settled, and from which God later brought Israel out.

moments.title: Abram goes down to Egypt
moments.text: A severe famine hit the land, so Abram went to Egypt for a while. He asked Sarai to say she was his sister, afraid the Egyptians would kill him for her.

moments.title: Jacob's family comes to Egypt
moments.text: Jacob's family came to Egypt, including two sons born to Joseph there. In all, seventy members of the family went to Egypt.

moments.title: The Nile turns to blood
moments.text: The fish in the Nile died and the river smelled so bad the Egyptians could not drink it. Egypt's magicians did the same, and Pharaoh's heart stayed hard.

moments.title: Isaiah's sign against Egypt
moments.text: The LORD had Isaiah go naked and barefoot for three years as a sign against Egypt and Cush. The king of Assyria would lead Egypt's captives away, and those who boasted in Egypt would be ashamed.

moments.title: A blessing for Egypt
moments.text: The LORD promised a day when Egypt and Assyria would worship together and join Israel in a blessing on the earth. He called Egypt "My people."

cards.name: Bethlehem
cards.line: Bethlehem is a town in Judah, also called Ephrath, near where Rachel was buried, where David's story began, and where a ruler for Israel was to come from.

moments.title: Rachel is buried
moments.text: Rachel died on the way to Ephrath, which is Bethlehem, and was buried there on the way. Jacob set up a pillar on her grave.

moments.title: Naomi and Ruth arrive
moments.text: Naomi came back from Moab with her daughter-in-law Ruth. They arrived in Bethlehem at the start of the barley harvest.

moments.title: Samuel visits Jesse
moments.text: Samuel did what the LORD had said and went to Bethlehem. The elders trembled and asked if he came in peace, and he said he came to sacrifice to the LORD.

moments.title: Water from the well
moments.text: David longed for water from the well near the gate of Bethlehem. Three mighty men broke through the Philistine camp to get it, but David poured it out to the LORD.

moments.title: Jesus is born in Bethlehem
moments.text: Jesus was born in Bethlehem in Judea, during the time of King Herod. The prophet had written that a ruler who would shepherd God's people Israel would come out of Bethlehem.

cards.name: Mount of Olives
cards.line: The Mount of Olives is a ridge east of Jerusalem where David wept, Jesus prayed and rode toward the city, and the LORD will one day stand.

moments.title: David weeps and climbs
moments.text: David climbed the Mount of Olives weeping, with his head covered and his feet bare. All the people with him covered their heads and wept too.

moments.title: The LORD will stand here
moments.text: Zechariah says that on that day the LORD's feet will stand on the Mount of Olives, east of Jerusalem. The mountain will split in two, forming a great valley.

moments.title: Jesus sends for a donkey
moments.text: Near Jerusalem, at the Mount of Olives, Jesus sent two disciples to bring a colt. As He rode, the crowd praised God for the miracles they had seen, and called Him the King who comes in the Lord's name.

moments.title: A hymn, then the mountain
moments.text: After the Last Supper, Jesus and His disciples sang a hymn and went out to the Mount of Olives. There Jesus said they would all fall away, and Peter said he never would.

moments.title: Jesus prays on the mountain
moments.text: Jesus went to the Mount of Olives as usual. He knelt and prayed, "Not My will, but Yours be done," and an angel strengthened Him.

cards.name: Patmos
cards.line: Patmos is a small, rocky island in the Aegean Sea where John was living when he received the vision written down in the book of Revelation.

moments.title: John on Patmos
moments.text: John calls himself a brother and partner in the troubles, the kingdom, and the patient endurance found in Jesus. He says he was on the island of Patmos because of the word of God and his testimony about Jesus.

moments.title: A voice like a trumpet
moments.text: On the Lord's day, John was in the Spirit and heard a loud voice behind him like a trumpet. It told him to write what he saw and send it to seven churches.

moments.title: One like the Son of Man
moments.text: After John heard the voice on Patmos, he turned and saw seven golden lampstands. Among them stood One like the Son of Man, with white hair, eyes like blazing fire, and a voice like the roar of many waters.

cards.name: Lebanon
cards.line: Lebanon is a mountain region north of Israel, famous for its tall cedar trees, and the Bible names it as promised land and a source of building wood.

moments.title: Part of the promised land
moments.text: At Horeb, God tells Israel to go and take the land He promised, reaching to Lebanon and the great River Euphrates.

moments.title: God's promise for Lebanon
moments.text: God tells Joshua that land is still left to take, including all Lebanon to the east. He promises that He Himself will drive out the people of the Lebanon hill country before Israel.

moments.title: Wood from Lebanon for the temple
moments.text: Solomon sends word that he wants cedar, cypress, and algum logs from Lebanon. He says the king's servants are skilled at cutting timber there.

moments.title: Logs for the second temple
moments.text: After the exile, the people give food, drink, and oil to workers from Sidon and Tyre, who bring cedar logs from Lebanon to Joppa by sea. Cyrus king of Persia had given his permission.

moments.title: A prophecy about proud cedars
moments.text: Isaiah says a day is coming when the LORD will come against everything proud, including the tall cedars of Lebanon. On that day only the LORD will be lifted up.

cards.name: Ararat
cards.line: Ararat is a mountain region where Noah's ark came to rest after the Flood, and later a land named when God called nations against Babylon.

moments.title: The ark comes to rest
moments.text: The waters went down for 150 days. On the seventeenth day of the seventh month, the ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat.

cards.name: Holy Place
cards.line: The Holy Place was the room inside the tabernacle and later the temple, set apart for serving God and separated from the Most Holy Place by a veil.

moments.title: A veil divides the rooms
moments.text: God told Moses to hang a veil and put the ark of the Testimony behind it. The veil would separate the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place.

moments.title: Priests wear special clothes
moments.text: Aaron and his sons had to wear linen undergarments when they served in the Holy Place, so that they would not become guilty and die.

moments.title: The cloud fills the house
moments.text: When the priests came out of the Holy Place, a cloud filled the house of the LORD. The priests could not stand to serve, because the glory of the LORD filled it.

moments.title: The service is neglected
moments.text: The king said that their fathers had shut the doors of the portico and put out the lamps. They did not burn incense or present burnt offerings in the Holy Place of the God of Israel.

cards.name: Tarshish
cards.line: Tarshish was a far-off place across the sea, known for its ships and rich cargo, and it is where Jonah tried to run when he fled from the LORD.

moments.title: Kings of Tarshish bring tribute
moments.text: A prayer for the king asks that the kings of Tarshish and distant shores bring tribute. It puts Tarshish among the far places whose rulers bring gifts.

moments.title: Wail, ships of Tarshish
moments.text: Isaiah speaks against Tyre and calls on the ships of Tarshish to wail, because Tyre is laid waste, without house or harbor.

moments.title: Daughter of Tarshish
moments.text: Isaiah spoke against Tyre and called to the Daughter of Tarshish. He said there was no longer a harbor.

moments.title: Silver from Tarshish
moments.text: Jeremiah says hammered silver is brought from Tarshish. A craftsman works it into idols, but the LORD is the true God.

moments.title: Ships of Tarshish carry cargo
moments.text: Ezekiel says the ships of Tarshish carried Tyre's merchandise. Tyre was filled with heavy cargo in the heart of the sea.

cards.name: Rephidim
cards.line: Rephidim was a camp in the wilderness where Israel found no water, fought the Amalekites, and then left to go on to the Wilderness of Sinai.

moments.title: No water to drink
moments.text: Israel camped at Rephidim, but there was no water. The people argued with Moses, and God told him to strike the rock at Horeb so water would come out for them.

moments.title: The Amalekites attack
moments.text: The Amalekites attacked Israel at Rephidim. Israel prevailed while Moses held up his hands, and Aaron and Hur held them steady until sunset, so Joshua overwhelmed Amalek with the sword.

moments.title: Leaving for Sinai
moments.text: After Israel set out from Rephidim, they entered the Wilderness of Sinai and camped in front of the mountain.

cards.name: Tarsus
cards.line: Tarsus was a well-known city in Cilicia and the hometown of Saul, who became the apostle Paul, and it is where he was sent and later sought out.

moments.title: Ananias asks for a man from Tarsus
moments.text: The Lord tells Ananias to go to Judas' house on Straight Street in Damascus. There he is to ask for a man from Tarsus named Saul, who is praying.

moments.title: Barnabas looks for Saul
moments.text: Barnabas goes to Tarsus to look for Saul. When he finds him, he brings him back to Antioch, and they teach large numbers of people there.

moments.title: Paul names his hometown
moments.text: Paul tells a crowd he is a Jew from Tarsus in Cilicia, a citizen of no ordinary city. He then asks to speak to the people, and tells them he was born in Tarsus.

cards.name: Kiriath-jearim
cards.line: Kiriath-jearim was a city on the border of Judah and Benjamin, best known as the place where the ark of the LORD stayed for twenty years.

moments.title: A city of the Gibeonites
moments.text: After the Israelites learned the Gibeonites lived nearby, they went to their cities. Kiriath-jearim was one of them.

moments.title: A border city
moments.text: Kiriath-jearim, also called Baalah and Kiriath-baal, marked part of the border of Judah. It was also on the edge of Benjamin's land.

moments.title: The Danites camp here
moments.text: Six hundred Danites went up and camped at Kiriath-jearim. The place west of it was called Mahaneh-dan.

moments.title: The ark comes to Kiriath-jearim
moments.text: The Philistines sent back the ark, and the men of Kiriath-jearim came for it. They took it to Abinadab's house on the hill and set apart his son Eleazar to guard it, and it stayed there twenty years.

moments.title: David brings the ark out
moments.text: David gathered all Israel and went up to Kiriath-jearim to bring up the ark of God. Later, he brought it to the tent he had pitched in Jerusalem.

cards.name: Succoth
cards.line: Succoth was a city east of the Jordan where Jacob built shelters for his livestock, and where Gideon later punished leaders who refused to help his tired troops.

moments.title: Jacob builds a home
moments.text: Jacob went on to Succoth. There he built a house for himself and shelters for his livestock, and that is why the place was called Succoth.

moments.title: Land in the valley
moments.text: Succoth was named among the cities in the valley on the east side of the Jordan. It was part of the territory of King Sihon of Heshbon.

moments.title: Gideon is refused bread
moments.text: Gideon asked the men of Succoth for bread for his worn-out troops. The leaders refused, asking if he already had the two Midianite kings in his hands.

moments.title: Gideon returns
moments.text: Gideon captured a young man of Succoth, who wrote down the names of seventy-seven leaders and elders. Gideon then took the elders and disciplined the men of Succoth with the thorns and briers of the wilderness.

cards.name: Jabbok
cards.line: The Jabbok is a stream east of the Jordan River where Jacob wrestled and was renamed Israel, and later a border mark for Israel and the Ammonites.

moments.title: Jacob crosses the river
moments.text: During the night Jacob took his two wives, his two servant women, and his eleven sons and crossed the shallow crossing place of the Jabbok. He sent them across the stream with all his things.

moments.title: Israel's land reaches the Jabbok
moments.text: After Israel defeated Sihon, they took his land from the Arnon to the Jabbok. They went no farther than the border of the Ammonites, because their land was protected by strong walls.

moments.title: Land along the Jabbok left alone
moments.text: Moses reminded Israel that they did not go near the land along the banks of the Jabbok River. The LORD had forbidden it.

moments.title: The Jabbok marks the border
moments.text: Moses gave the Reubenites and Gadites land from Gilead to the Arnon Valley and up to the Jabbok River. The Jabbok was the border of the Ammonites.

moments.title: Jephthah answers the Ammonites
moments.text: The Ammonite king said Israel had taken his land from the Arnon to the Jabbok. Jephthah replied that the LORD had driven out the Amorites and given the land to Israel.

cards.name: Sheep Gate
cards.line: The Sheep Gate was a gate in Jerusalem's wall, rebuilt by priests in Nehemiah's day, and it was near the pool of Bethesda where Jesus healed a man.

moments.title: Priests start the work
moments.text: Eliashib the high priest and his fellow priests began rebuilding at the Sheep Gate. They dedicated it and installed its doors.

moments.title: Goldsmiths and merchants repair
moments.text: The goldsmiths and merchants made repairs on the wall between the upper room above the corner and the Sheep Gate.

moments.title: Thanksgiving walk on the wall
moments.text: On the day of thanksgiving, a choir and Nehemiah with half the people walked along the top of the wall as far as the Sheep Gate. Then they stopped at the Gate of the Guard.

moments.title: Jesus at the pool nearby
moments.text: A pool called Bethesda was near the Sheep Gate, and many sick people lay there. Jesus told a man who had been sick for thirty-eight years to get up, pick up his mat, and walk.

cards.name: Tirzah
cards.line: Tirzah was an old Canaanite city that later became a royal home for the kings of northern Israel, where kings reigned, fell, and died.

moments.title: A king of Tirzah is listed
moments.text: The king of Tirzah is named as one of the kings in a list. The verse says there were thirty-one kings in all.

moments.title: Jeroboam's son dies
moments.text: Jeroboam's wife went to Tirzah. As soon as she stepped over the threshold of the house, the boy died.

moments.title: Baasha reigns in Tirzah
moments.text: Baasha became king of all Israel in the third year of Asa's reign over Judah. He reigned in Tirzah twenty-four years.

moments.title: Zimri kills Elah
moments.text: King Elah was in Tirzah getting drunk when his servant Zimri plotted against him. Zimri killed him and reigned in his place.

moments.title: Omri surrounds Tirzah
moments.text: Omri and the Israelites marched up and surrounded Tirzah. When Zimri saw the city was captured, he burned the royal palace down upon himself.

cards.name: Kibroth-hattaavah
cards.line: Kibroth-hattaavah was a camp in the wilderness where Israel buried people who craved other food, and its name means graves of craving.

moments.title: Graves of craving
moments.text: While the people were still eating the meat, the LORD's anger burned and He struck them with a severe plague. They named the place Kibroth-hattaavah because they buried the people who had craved other food there.

moments.title: A stop on the journey
moments.text: Israel set out from the Wilderness of Sinai and camped at Kibroth-hattaavah. Then they moved on and camped at Hazeroth.

moments.title: Moving on to Hazeroth
moments.text: From Kibroth-hattaavah the people moved on to Hazeroth, where they remained for some time.

moments.title: Making the LORD angry
moments.text: At Kibroth-hattaavah, Israel made the LORD angry. They did the same at Taberah and at Massah.

cards.name: Forest of Ephraim
cards.line: The Forest of Ephraim was a wooded region where David's army fought Israel, and where Absalom, David's son, was caught in an oak tree.

moments.title: Battle in the forest
moments.text: David's army marched out to fight Israel, and the battle took place in the forest of Ephraim. Israel was defeated, and twenty thousand men died that day.

moments.title: The forest devours
moments.text: The battle spread over the whole countryside. That day the forest devoured more people than the sword.

moments.title: Absalom caught in the oak
moments.text: Absalom was riding his mule under the thick branches of a large oak. His head caught fast in the tree, and the mule kept going, leaving him hanging in midair.

cards.name: En-rogel
cards.line: En-rogel was a spring near Jerusalem that marked a border between Judah and Benjamin, and it was a place of secret messages and a royal feast.

moments.title: A border marker
moments.text: En-rogel is named as a point where the border of Judah ran, and it also appears in the border of Benjamin, near the southern slope of the Jebusites (Jerusalem).

moments.title: Waiting for news
moments.text: Jonathan and Ahimaaz stayed at En-rogel because they dared not be seen entering the city. A servant girl brought them news, and they passed it on to King David.

moments.title: Adonijah's feast
moments.text: Adonijah sacrificed sheep, oxen, and fattened calves near the stone of Zoheleth, next to En-rogel. He invited his royal brothers and the men of Judah who served the king, but not Nathan, Benaiah, or Solomon.

cards.name: El-elohe-Israel
cards.line: El-Elohe-Israel is the name Jacob gave to an altar he set up near Shechem on land he bought, and Schaff's Dictionary says it means "strength of God."

moments.title: Jacob buys the land
moments.text: Jacob bought the plot of ground where he had pitched his tent. He paid the sons of Hamor, Shechem's father, a hundred pieces of silver.

moments.title: An altar is set up
moments.text: There Jacob set up an altar and called it El-Elohe-Israel.
